referents.why: 'to them' (autois), masculine plural: the people for whom the release was made. No candidate in this verse is the people; the crowd first appears in 15:8.
'whom' (hon), masculine singular relative, agrees with 'prisoner' in the noun phrase it modifies.
'he used to release' has Pilate as subject; the verse names Pilate's custom. Mrk.15.5#w9 is Pilate, the masculine singular nearest.
'they requested': the plural requesters are the people. No candidate in this verse or the verses before is the people.

links.why: Self-link: a clause cannot follow itself.
The relative clause whom they requested sits inside the noun phrase 'one prisoner', the object of cl0. The within role carries it.

none_fit.what: A background aside about Pilate's custom before the next event. The only cross-verse link is and, which does not mark background.

cant_tell.what: Who the people are in this verse.
cant_tell.why: The Greek gives only pronouns for them. The crowd is named only in Mrk.15.8, so both pronouns are left as none.

cant_tell.what: referents of to them (w4) and they (cl1s): the people, the crowd
cant_tell.why: the people are named in the English but not by a noun in this verse; the crowd (w3) is a candidate only in verse 8
